entities.name: Afar National Democratic Party
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Afar National Democratic Party (ANDP), the main political party representing the Afar people — a Cushitic ethnic group of approximately 3-5 million inhabiting the Afar Triangle (the desert lowlands where Ethiopia, Eritrea, and Djibouti meet, including the Danakil Depression) — emerged in the post-1991 Ethiopian federal political reorganization under the EPRDF system and has served as the ruling party of the Afar Regional State in Ethiopia, one of the country's nine ethnic federal units.

The Afar people are historically significant beyond their numbers: the Afar Triangle is one of the most geologically active regions on Earth (the Danakil Depression reaches 100 meters below sea level, where three tectonic plates are pulling apart) and is the site of the most ancient hominid fossils including 'Lucy' (Australopithecus afarensis, 3.2 million years old). The Afar have maintained a nomadic pastoral tradition in one of the world's hottest and most inhospitable environments.

The ANDP operated within the EPRDF's ethnic federal framework, which divided Ethiopia into ethnically-defined regional states with their own governments. This system — created by Meles Zenawi to manage Ethiopia's ethnic diversity — gave the Afar Regional State formal autonomy while keeping it within a controlled federal structure. After Abiy Ahmed's 2018 reforms dissolving the EPRDF into the Prosperity Party, many ethnic regional parties including ANDP faced pressure to join the new national party. The Afar region has been affected by the Tigray War (2020-2022) and ongoing drought and development challenges.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Afar National Democratic Party — representing one of Africa's most ancient and geologically significant regions, operating within Ethiopia's ethnic federal system, and navigating the Tigray War's humanitarian impact on Afar territory — is an institution of regional importance in the Horn of Africa's political development.
